newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing share market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing share market report.

text.p: Dutch shares closed down on Wednesday after a lower Wall Street opening blocked uptrend in the middle of the afternoon.
The Dutch AEX share index, closed 1.31 points lower at 587.84, after hitting an intra-day high of 590.76 points.
Dealers said the advance earlier was hesitant and a further correction on Wall Street could halt recent upswing. "But sentiment remains good in the longer run," said one dealer.
Philips outperformed the market and added 1.30 guilders to 64.10. Another index heavyweight, Royal Dutch dropped 3.80 guilders to 279.60 on profit taking after recent rise.
One dealer said the dip for Royal Dutch was just temporary.

"The nearer the stock crawls to the 300 guilders per share, the more likely it is the share will be split," he said, adding there were rumours in the market. "A share split will increase turnover," he added.
Dealers could not clarify why Nutricia rose 4.10 guilders to 239.10, surpassing yesterday's closing high.

High-tech funds gained since yesterday's U.S. book-to-bill ratio announcement, a key indicator for the semiconductor industry. The ratio rose to 0.99 in September from 0.93 in August, "This increased investors confidence for Philips."
Among the smaller high tech stocks Simac showed a new all time high at 72.50 guilders, a rise of 5.50 guilders.
Anglo-Dutch Computer Management Group (CMG) rose 0.80 guilders to 21.00, also surpassing an earlier closing high.
Trading firm Hagemeyer added 1.10 guilders to close at a new high of 138.00 guilders.
"The undertone in the market is positive," said one dealer, adding investors might stay sidelined in the next few days.
"They keep their powder dry as it is difficult to foresee which stocks will outperform the market after the recent upswing," he said.
"I do not expect big jumps," he said, adding air carrier KLM might have bottomed out.
